_comment: Golden expectations for tests/run.py: every score quoted in a README is here and is re-measured by tests/run.py (area_mge and depth exactly, and the gate mix).

Per task: `references` (tasks/<task>/reference/<stem>.sv; accepted by check.py with <stem>.lean, or for a draft task the `stage` check.py stops at with the draft's partial Lean file), `baselines` (tests/<task>/baselines/<stem>.sv unless `sv` says otherwise, relative to tests/<task>/; scored only, never accepted: `banned` says whether the task's banlist rejects it, the score is taken with the banlist lifted), `negatives` (tests/<task>/negative/<stem>.sv; rejected by check.py at `stage` when submitted with the task's first reference proof).

`scores` maps a parameter point (`N=16`, or `default` for a parameterless top) to the pinned flow's result there (score/score.py: score/svgolf.ys + score/ge.json, Yosys 0.53). Regenerate the scores with `python3.12 tests/run.py --update-scores` after a deliberate change of the flow. `flow` pins that combinational flow and `flow_seq` the clocked one (score/svgolf_seq.ys + score/ge_seq.json, the same Yosys and canon.ys): the boards compare a record with the pin of its task's kind (decided 2026-11-07).

`attacks` (tests/<task>/attacks/<stem>.sv; through `check.py --unproved`, or with a reference proof when `lean` says so: `reference` the task's first, `reference/<stem>.lean` that one; rejected at `stage`): optional `message_contains` (a phrase the rejection must carry, or a list of phrases of which it must carry one, with the reason in `why`; WP-C3's `design` rejections name the unsupported construct), `postsynth_alone` (`rejects` | `passes`: the postsynth check alone with the source gate and the fourstate stage bypassed), `postsynth_mode` (`light` when absent; `full` for an attack that ONLY the full post-synthesis check rejects: the mode of the check.py run and of the `postsynth_alone` run, WP-C2), `postsynth_light` (the LIGHT mode's own verdict where it is documented, `rejects` | `passes`), `functional` and `tactics` (the advisory checks). `advisory` (true): a test of the checker's own behavior that the refusal register (docs/sv-refusals.json, tools/gen_sv_refusals.py) does not need to cite; WP-C2/WP-C3 set it on `func_call`, `assign_func` and `rare_mid` until the register has entries for them.

extra_in.message_contains: the inputs are ['a', 'b', 'en'] (in declaration order), the task's are ['a', 'b']
extra_in.why: hidden extra input; refuted in negative/Refute.lean (extraIn_refuted). Since 2026-11-07 check.py rejects it at extract, before any proof: its ports at the probe points are not task.json's (`port_problems`, the statement's Interface at those points).

arith_and.why: correct function through banned run-time + and -

casex_item.why: `s = 1'b0; case (s) 1'bx: y = '0; default: y = a & b;`: ls-sv computes a & b, Yosys reads the x item as matching and drives x (0 GE). The source gate refuses the x literal digit; before that rule it passed every stage up to postsynth (LIVE), and postsynth alone still rejects every vector.

zpair_or.why: complementary z case items `2'b0z`, `2'b1z` on {a[0], b[0]}: none matches in ls-sv (a & b), together they match every input in Yosys (a | b). Refused by the source gate (x/z literal digits); postsynth alone rejects nearly every vector.

z_rare.why: `case ({a, b}) 32'hDEAD_BEEz: y = '0;`: Yosys drops the z bits, so the netlist outputs 0 on 2^-28 of the inputs, ls-sv never. Refused by the source gate; postsynth alone rejects it only through the harvested constant's 0/1 bits (x/z bits left free), never by random vectors.

zconst_param.why: the x/z bits inside localparams built by concatenation, `{1'b0, 1'bz}` and `{1'b1, 1'bx}`, as case items: a & b in ls-sv, a | b in Yosys. Refused by the source gate (the literal digits); postsynth alone rejects.

zeq_pair_if.why: `if ((a[1:0] == 2'b0z) || (a[1:0] == 2'b1z))`: x in ls-sv (else branch, a & b), always true in Yosys (a | b). Refused by the source gate; postsynth alone rejects.

param_divzero.why: an x without an x literal: `localparam logic [1:0] K = 2'd1 / 2'd0;` (constant division is not banned) as a case item: never matches in ls-sv (a & b), matches every input in Yosys (a | b). Refused by the fourstate stage (a parameter with unknown bits, slang's DivisionByZero); postsynth alone rejects.

undriven_mux.why: `logic u; t = u ? 0 : 1; if (t) y = a | b; else y = a & b;`: u is x in ls-sv (else branch, a & b), a don't-care Yosys resolves to t = 1 (a | b). Refused by the fourstate stage (Yosys `check`: used but no driver); postsynth alone rejects.

undriven_offpoint.why: ATTACK (the universal-correctness audit, 2026-11-06): undriven_mux's undriven `u`, driven only at N = 16 by a generate-if: ls-sv computes a & b at every N, the pinned flow's N = 8 netlist a | b. Every stage passed it at the scoring point; refused since the fourstate stage runs at every point the checker probes (here N = 1); postsynth alone, which runs at the scoring point only, passes it

oob_select.why: `k[{1'b1, a[1:0]}]` always reads past k's 4 bits (x): else branch (a & b) in ls-sv, t = 1 (a | b) in Yosys. Refused by the fourstate stage (a run-time index that can leave the range); postsynth alone rejects.

oob_rare.why: the out-of-range read confined to ONE input pair (a = 16'hAAAA, b = 16'hB6DB, a reduction-AND detector): ls-sv a & b everywhere, the netlist flips y[0] there. Refused exactly by the fourstate stage; postsynth alone PASSES it (2^-32 of the inputs, no comparison constant to harvest): the sampling limit the static refusals exist for.

fn_uninit.why: LATENT: a function-local `logic r;` read before it is assigned: x in IEEE (else branch, a & b), resolved to 1 by Yosys (a | b). No static rule sees it (no literal, Yosys `check` passes); ls-sv has no user function calls yet, so the design LOADS with an Unsupported node, no proof about it can hold, and the `design` stage rejects it (WP-C3: `Design2.hasUnsupported`, naming the first loud node; before WP-C3 it surfaced only at the postsynth stage, which failed closed on it, and the postsynth check alone still does). A PR that adds function calls must add a 4-state rule for unassigned locals first.

latch_never.why: LATENT: an `always_latch` that is never enabled keeps its initial x in IEEE (`!r` is x: else branch, a & b); Yosys resolves the never-loaded latch to 0 (`!r` = 1: a | b, 21.328 GE). No static rule sees it (no literal; the latch is a driver, so Yosys `check` passes); ls-sv does not run `always_latch`, so the design loads with an Unsupported process and the `design` stage rejects it (WP-C3; before it, the postsynth stage failed closed on it, and the postsynth check alone still does). A PR that adds `always_latch` must add a 4-state rule for a latch's initial x first. (10/30 night: since the off-prem agent's extractor commit 'admit always_ff and always_latch' the envelope carries an `AlwaysLatch` process that the symbolic loader does not know yet, so the rejection comes from `load_design_sv2` itself with `unknown process kind "AlwaysLatch"` at the same `design` stage; the earlier WP-C3 message for this design is the one `latch_star` and `fn_uninit` still show.) Since WP-PROC follow-up 3 (2026-11-01) rule (e) of score/fourstate.py refuses every latch Yosys's `proc` infers (`select -assert-none t:$dlatch t:$adlatch t:$dlatchsr`) and that stage runs before `design`: the attack now stops at `fourstate`, naming the latched signal `r` (the `design` rejection above is what it was before, and what the design stage would still say).

latch_star.why: LATENT: the same never-loaded latch written with `always @*` (Yosys's `proc` infers it without the error it gives for `always_comb`): x in IEEE (a & b), 0 in Yosys (a | b). No static rule sees it; ls-sv runs `always @*` only under the rules R1 to R6 of docs/sv-proc-lowering.md (WP-PROC E1, 2026-11-01): R5 refuses a block that assigns a variable on some paths only, so the design still loads with an Unsupported process (`TimedStatement:ImplicitEventControl`, text names R5) and the `design` stage rejects it (WP-C3; before it, the postsynth stage failed closed). The Yosys-side assertion that no `$dlatch` exists after `proc` (defense in depth for R5, design note PROC-NOTE section 7) is rule (e) of score/fourstate.py since WP-PROC follow-up 3 (2026-11-01), and `fourstate` runs before `design`: the attack now stops at `fourstate` (`proc` inferred a latch for `r`), where both rules refuse it.

unique_nomatch.why: `unique case` that never matches: the source gate refuses `unique`; with the gate bypassed, postsynth rejects every vector (Yosys: x, 0 GE).

priority_nomatch.why: `priority case` that never matches: as unique_nomatch.

unique_overlap.why: `unique case (1'b1) a[1]: ...; a[0]: ...;` overlapping items: Yosys's parallel_case ORs both arms where both match; with the gate bypassed, postsynth rejects about a quarter of the vectors.

unique_rare.why: unique_overlap confined to `a[7:0] == 8'hEF && b == 16'h1234` (2^-24 of the inputs): with the gate bypassed, postsynth rejects it only through the harvested comparison constants.

unique_first_const.why: benign-looking `unique case (1'b1)` whose first item is the constant 1: the netlist is a & b. Refused by the source gate. With the gate bypassed, postsynth REJECTS since master 2218821b (ls-sv 0.1.424, 2026-11-02): whenever a[0]=1 both items match, a `unique` violation, and run2 now returns a loud CaseCheck result on such a settled state instead of silently taking the first item. So the model and the netlist differ on those vectors (117 of 256 in light mode). Before, postsynth alone found no difference. The svGolf X10 finding asked for exactly this.

unique0_nomatch.why: benign `unique0 case` that never matches (parallel_case only): the netlist is a & b; with the gate bypassed, postsynth finds no difference.

for_counter_write.why: a procedural for loop writing its own counter (`k = int'(a[0])`): Yosys ignores the write (y = a & b, 21 GE), simulation loops forever when a[0] = 0. Under `_example`'s arithmetic ban the banlist rejects the loop's `k++` (a counter the body writes is run-time); without that ban the design stage would (the ls-sv loader refuses the envelope's `LocalDecl` statement). postsynth alone fails closed (ls-sv cannot evaluate it).

for_counter_skip.why: a for loop skipping an iteration by `k = k + 1`: simulation gives a & b, Yosys ignores the write and drives 0 (0 GE). The banlist rejects the run-time `+` on a counter the body writes; postsynth alone fails closed (ls-sv refuses the loop).

array_sum.why: `arr.sum()` on an unpacked array: the banlist's front check flags the array reduction method (run-time `+`); Yosys 0.53 cannot read the method (the backstop fails too).

func_call.message_contains: every check that needs no proof passed
func_call.why: WP-C3 fixture, superseded 2026-11-02: a CORRECT `a & b` written through a user function called from always_comb. It used to load with a loud Unsupported node and be rejected at `design`. The symbolic tier now inlines pure input-only functions (USERFN), so the design runs, passes every check that needs no proof, and post-synthesis agrees with ls-sv. The design-stage refusal stays covered by fn_uninit and clmul's gen_local_column, always_star_rows and verilog2001_wire.

assign_func.message_contains: every check that needs no proof passed
assign_func.why: WP-C3 fixture, superseded 2026-11-02: the same function call in a continuous assignment (`assign y = both(a, b)`). Inlined by the symbolic tier now (USERFN); it passes every check that needs no proof, like func_call.

rare_mid.why: WP-C2: the out-of-range read confined to about 2^-9 of the inputs (the low 9 bits of a equal a fixed pattern, a reduction-AND detector with no comparison constant to harvest): ls-sv a & b everywhere, the netlist flips y[0] there. Refused exactly by the fourstate stage. The FULL postsynth check alone rejects it (7 of 4130 vectors, all random), the LIGHT one passes it (256 vectors, 191 random): the sampling boundary between the two modes, the one attack only the full check catches.

add_n_sklansky.why: Sklansky parallel prefix; simulation only (validate/validate.py, verilator.py, postsynth.py), no proof yet

add_n_kogge_stone.why: Kogge-Stone parallel prefix; simulation only (validate/validate.py, verilator.py, postsynth.py), no proof yet

cmp_carry.why: every carry a run-time comparison, which alumacc builds as Yosys's own adder ($alu): banned run-time ordering comparisons in a task that bans + and - (decided 2026-11-05; scored with the banlist lifted); simulation only (validate/validate.py, postsynth.py)

plus.why: Yosys's own `assign {cout, s} = a + b + cin;` (banned run-time +; scored with the banlist lifted): the baseline to beat

no_cin.why: carry in ignored (c[0] = 0); refuted in negative/Refute.lean (noCin_refuted)

cout_off.why: off-by-one carry out (cout = c[N-1]); refuted in negative/Refute.lean (coutOff_refuted)

carry_bug.why: wrong carry gate ((a & b) | (c & a)); refuted in negative/Refute.lean (carryBug_refuted)

only_n16.why: a ripple adder at N = 16 only (the scoring point; it scores like the reference there), carry-free elsewhere; refuted in negative/Refute.lean (onlyN16_refuted)

wide_s.message_contains: the outputs are ['s'] (in declaration order), the task's are ['s', 'cout']
wide_s.why: interface: one (N+1)-bit output s = {cout, sum}, no cout port; refuted in negative/Refute.lean (wideS_refuted). Since 2026-11-07 check.py rejects it at extract, before any proof: its ports at the probe points are not task.json's (`port_problems`, the statement's Interface at those points).

cin_name.message_contains: the inputs are ['a', 'b', 'ci'] (in declaration order), the task's are ['a', 'b', 'cin']
cin_name.why: interface: the carry in is named ci; refuted in negative/Refute.lean (cinName_refuted). Since 2026-11-07 check.py rejects it at extract, before any proof: its ports at the probe points are not task.json's (`port_problems`, the statement's Interface at those points).

dead_clock.why: a correct sum registered by always_ff on a clock nothing drives: right in every ls-sv snapshot, x in every simulator, 0 GE. The fourstate stage refuses it first (Yosys `check`: `clk` is used but has no driver); the loader's clock discipline (Clock:source) refuses it too, so the kernel-checked refutation through Unclocked (deadClock_refuted) is retired (there is no `.sem` to refute)

dead_clock_tied.why: the same with the clock tied to 1'b0. Since WP-Q0 the loader itself refuses a clock that is not an input port (Clock:source, LeanModels/Sv/ClockGuard2.lean), so the design stage rejects it before any proof; the kernel-checked refutation through the Unclocked conjunct (deadClockTied_refuted) is retired because there is no `.sem` to refute (the generic not_satisfiedAt_of_clocked remains in negative/Refute.lean)

plus.why: the right function through banned run-time + (Yosys's own adder, the baseline)

add_proc_case.why: a CORRECT ripple adder whose carry cell is an always_comb `case` with an arm in `begin … end`: every design check passes, but such an arm is outside the fragment of the sv_comb tactics (a plain `case` with single-assignment arms and a `default` is inside since WP-G S3a), so sv_structure in the proof file (the add_proc reference proof) logs its refusal and admits the goal. check.py must reject it at the solution stage: an error from the new tactic elaborators plus an admitted goal can never be accepted (the compile error, and sorryAx in the axiom check)
add_proc_case.message_contains: `case` arm is not a single assignment

z_case_item.why: a correct ripple sum behind `case (cin) 1'bz: ... default: s = sr;`: ls-sv computes the sum (case items compare by ===, like a 4-state simulator: Icarus 12, measured 10/28), Yosys reads the z item as a don't-care match and drives x (0 GE). The source gate refuses the z literal digit; before that rule it was LIVE (it passed every stage up to postsynth, and only a proof stood between it and a 0 GE entry), and postsynth alone still rejects every vector.

eqx_x.why: `(cin === 1'bx) ? '0 : sum`: Yosys folds it to the constant 0 (0 GE) where a 4-state simulator computes the sum (Icarus 12, measured 10/28); ls-sv has no `===` yet. Refused by the source gate (the x literal digit); postsynth alone fails closed (ls-sv cannot evaluate the design).

eqx_undriven.why: `(u === cin)` with `u` undriven: Yosys folds it to 0 (0 GE). Refused by the fourstate stage (Yosys `check`: `u` is used but has no driver); postsynth alone fails closed (ls-sv has no `===`).

slang_two_always.why: multiple-always-assigns: two always_comb writers of `cout` (IEEE 1800-2023 9.2.2.2, 9.2.2.4). Decided 2026-11-01: "slang reports a program illegal" means the FULL slang driver, analysis errors included (`Compilation.getAllDiagnostics()`, which banlist and fourstate read, omits them): the banlist front check now reads them (score/slangdriver.py). Before: both blocks drive the same value, so Yosys `check` and fourstate passed it and only the Lean `driversOk` guard refused it, at the `design` stage.

slang_mixed_assign.why: mixed-var-assigns: `assign cout` plus `always_comb cout` (IEEE 1800-2023 6.5). Decided 2026-11-01: "slang reports a program illegal" means the FULL slang driver, analysis errors included (`Compilation.getAllDiagnostics()`, which banlist and fourstate read, omits them): the banlist front check now reads them (score/slangdriver.py). Before: same values on both drivers, so fourstate passed it and only the Lean guard refused it, at the `design` stage.

slang_input_assign.why: `assign cin = a[0]`: cannot assign to input port (IEEE 1800-2023 23.3.3.2). Decided 2026-11-01: "slang reports a program illegal" means the FULL slang driver, analysis errors included (`Compilation.getAllDiagnostics()`, which banlist and fourstate read, omits them): the banlist front check now reads them (score/slangdriver.py). Before: refused at fourstate, only because Yosys `check` reports two drivers of `a`'s bit.

slang_initial_comb.why: an `initial` block and an `always_comb` writing `cout`: multiple-always-assigns (IEEE 1800-2023 9.2.2.2; Xcelium *E,MULAXX; Yosys accepts the netlist). Decided 2026-11-01: "slang reports a program illegal" means the FULL slang driver, analysis errors included (`Compilation.getAllDiagnostics()`, which banlist and fourstate read, omits them): the banlist front check now reads them (score/slangdriver.py). Before: refused only at the `design` stage, because the Lean loader has no `Initial` process kind (docs/sv-tools-split-audit.md section 5, finding 2); a day `initial` is admitted it would have passed every stage.

slang_always_notime.why: `always cout = c[N];` never advances time: 'always' procedure does not advance time (IEEE 1800-2023 9.2.2.1, a simulation deadlock; Yosys reads a wire). Decided 2026-11-01: "slang reports a program illegal" means the FULL slang driver, analysis errors included (`Compilation.getAllDiagnostics()`, which banlist and fourstate read, omits them): the banlist front check now reads them (score/slangdriver.py). Before: refused only at the `design` stage (the extractor's `ProceduralBlockSymbol:NoEventControl`), fourstate and banlist passed it.

zpair_add_rare.why: complementary z items on {a[0], cin} around a ripple adder whose z arms flip s[0] on ONE input pair (a = 16'hAAAA, b = 16'hB6DB, a reduction-AND detector): ls-sv computes the sum everywhere (provable), the netlist is wrong on that pair. Refused exactly by the source gate; postsynth alone PASSES it (found by the round-2 review): the sampling limit the static refusals exist for.

wrong_carry.why: ADVISORY CHECK, not an attack on ls-sv/Yosys: a ripple adder whose carry drops the propagate term ((a & b) | (c & a)). ls-sv and the netlist agree, so it passes every stage before the proof (check.py --unproved stops at `unproved`, stage unchanged); the advisory functional smoke check (the task's oracle.py) finds 3245 of 4132 vectors wrong and adds ONE `warnings` line

mux_carry.why: ADVISORY CHECK (--tactics), not an attack: a CORRECT ripple adder with a `?:` carry, checker-legal. It WAS tactic-refused ("conditional expression `?:` (outside the v1 fragment)"); since WP-G S2 the conditional expression, `~ !`, the reductions, `&& ||` and `== !=` are in the sv_comb fragment (PROVING.md sections 4 and 14), so the same design is now INSIDE it (in_fragment true), kept as the regression for that; `+` and `-` are inside since WP-B2 (PROVING.md section 17); the refused shapes are the other word-level operators (`*`, `>`, shifts, unary minus) and a width conversion around an operation. The functional smoke check agrees with the oracle on every vector

localparam_carry.why: ADVISORY CHECK (--tactics), not an attack: a CORRECT ripple adder with a `localparam int M = N - 1;` read in an index, checker-legal. It WAS tactic-refused ("local parameters are outside the v1 fragment"); since the localparam extension (WP-F, PROVING.md section 4) a localparam of constant arithmetic over the parameters is one more named constant of the sv_comb summary, so the same design is now INSIDE the fragment (in_fragment true), kept as the regression for that; the refused shape is localparam_intdiv (localparam_clog2 is inside too). The functional smoke check agrees with the oracle on every vector

localparam_clog2.why: ADVISORY CHECK (--tactics), not an attack: a CORRECT ripple adder with a `localparam int L = $clog2(N + 1);` (the level count of the prefix-adder baselines), checker-legal. It WAS tactic-refused ("localparam `L`: `$clog2` is outside the v1 fragment"); since ls-sv admits an `int` localparam defined by `$clog2` (one more opaque named constant of the sv_comb summary; the instantiation evaluates it exactly, IEEE 1800-2023 20.8.1, and refuses a negative argument loudly), the same design is INSIDE the fragment (in_fragment true), kept as the regression for that; the refused shape is localparam_intdiv. The functional smoke check agrees with the oracle on every vector

localparam_intdiv.why: ADVISORY CHECK (--tactics), not an attack: a CORRECT ripple adder with a 2-state `localparam int H = (N + 1) / 2;`, checker-legal and tactic-refused (PROVING.md section 4: the extractor squashes a `/` or `%` under an `int` target to 2 states, which ls-sv reads as a wrap modulo 2^32, so the closed form would be false for huge N; the 4-state `localparam integer` is accepted); the functional smoke check agrees with the oracle on every vector

tactics_reference.why: ADVISORY CHECK (--tactics) on the proved reference: the sv_comb tactics read the design (in_fragment true, message ok), and the functional smoke check agrees with the oracle on every vector

hier_fa.why: ADVISORY CHECK (--tactics) on a correct ripple adder written with a `full_adder` module instance per bit (WP-I step I0): the design stage accepts it (the loader flattens), the sv_comb tactics have no summary for instances and the probe says so (`this design instantiates modules`), not 'cannot read a load_design_sv2 family' (measured: the design scores 112.0 GE / depth 33, exactly add_n)

tactics_proc.why: ADVISORY CHECK (--tactics) on the proved always_comb reference (WP-G): the plain sv_structure? refuses the procedural site, the second elaborator reads the LOWERED goal `exists d', (design.sem N).lowerComb = some d' /\ CombDesign d' /\ Acyclic d'` (in_fragment true, lowered true, message ok)

tactics_proc_case.why: ADVISORY CHECK (--tactics) on an always_comb body with a `case` whose arm is in `begin … end` (outside the fragment: a plain `case` with single-assignment arms and a `default` is inside since WP-G S3a): the answer is the second elaborator's refusal naming the construct, not the plain tactic's 'procedural process'

tactics.message_contains: `case` arm is not a single assignment

yosys_mul.why: Yosys's own `assign p = a * b;` (banned run-time *; scored with the banlist lifted): the baseline to beat

dadda_rc_8.why: Dadda tree + ripple final adder, generated for N = 8 only (gen_dadda.py 8)

dadda_rc_16.why: Dadda tree + ripple final adder, generated for N = 16 only (gen_dadda.py 16)

Its 8- and 16-bit siblings pass the check; N = 32 is not the scoring point.

dadda_ks_16.why: Dadda tree + Kogge-Stone final adder, generated for N = 16 only (gen_dadda.py 16 --final ks)

WRONG, independently of the proof: check.py --unproved --latency 16 (the clocked score) rejects it at postsynth, 63 failures at (3,4); the first: transaction 3 (alternating): output 0 is 15, want 0. the reference's proof (reference/sorter_ins.lean) fails at the solution stage (check.py with the reference proof, --no-score; every earlier stage passes) in so_static: the top process is not the reference's (unsolved goal False).

signed_order.why: the comparisons are signed (`$signed(in_data) > $signed(data[...])`, all three) instead of unsigned: values with the top bit set sort below the others and below the padding 0, so they are lost. Wrong for every N and W (at W = 1 the value 1 is -1). WRONG, independently of the proof: check.py --unproved --latency 16 (the clocked score) rejects it at postsynth, 57 failures at (3,4); the first: transaction 1 (one zero): output 1 is 0, want 15. the reference's proof (reference/sorter_ins.lean) fails at the solution stage (check.py with the reference proof, --no-score; every earlier stage passes), in so_static (the top process: unsolved goal False) and in cell_inst (`decide`).

rst_gate.why: the outputs are registered (ov_q, od_q) and out_valid is ov_q gated by the reset (`assign out_valid = ov_q & ~rst`; review L1 of 2026-11-08): every claimed snapshot is the reference's, but in the cycle of a reset entry the wire shows out_valid = 0 where the claimed snapshot before it shows a transaction's last output. Correct under the statement before 2026-11-09 (rule 1 exempted rst; check.py --unproved --postsynth full passes it: stage unproved, 0 failures at (3,4) and (8,8)); since 2026-11-09 rule 1 exempts nothing, and tests/sorter/negative/Refute.lean refutes it for every latency (rst_gate_refuted: the combinational path from rst to out_valid). The reference's proof (reference/sorter_ins.lean) fails at the solution stage (check.py with the reference proof, --no-score; every earlier stage passes), first in so_decls (the extra registers ov_q, od_q: unsolved goal False), then so_elems and so_static.

rr_mask.why: the proved reference (2026-11-05; reference/rr_mask.lean, every N with 1 <= N, N*N < 2^31, through SvGolf.ReactTask.satisfiedAt_of_rank): a registered mask round-robin, own code (the real-world candidate, OpenTitan prim_arbiter_tree behind an output register, tests/arbiter/designs/arbiter_ot.sv, waits on ls-sv's generate-local declarations: tasks/arbiter/README.md (l)). check.py ACCEPTS it (MEASURED 2026-11-05, cold, a fresh --stage-dir, --postsynth full): the clocked source rules, extraction and the design stage at the 5 probe points N = 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 (no unsupported construct), the solution stage 8.25 s, comparator and leanchecker (axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), the clocked score and the reactive post-synthesis check at N = 3, 5, 8 (3 seeds x 24 segments, the last 70000 entries long: 70 134 to 70 597 cycles per seed, 0 failures; the oracle binding, the Moore sample). The score: 769.488 um^2 x 2826 ps (one decision per cycle), 16 flops, 103 cells. RE-PROVED 2026-11-06 against the revised statement (txtask-v2's rules 2 and 3: the claims from every power-up state, TerminatesPU, XSafe; the design unchanged): rr_powerUp (every power-up state has the shape), rr_terminates (TerminatesPU.of_invariant), rr_xsafe (xsafeB by simp); check.py ACCEPTS it (MEASURED 2026-11-06, --postsynth full, a fresh --stage-dir): solution 4.79 s, comparator 13.3 s, leanchecker 15.3 s, the rule-3 twin and the never-loaded check pass, the reactive check at N = 3, 5, 8 from power-up states (seed 0 all zeros, seeds 1, 2 random on both sides), 70 134 to 70 597 cycles per seed, 0 failures; the score unchanged.

bit_ring.why: the universal-correctness audit (2026-11-06): the reference round-robin behind `if (&u)` on a never-reset 2-state 32-bit ring u (fixed priority when &u). ls-sv's own start gives a 2-state variable 0, so every run from it is fair and txtask-v1 accepted it; the scored netlist keeps u's 32 flops without an initial value and is fixed priority for ever from the power-up u = all ones. check.py rejects it at solution (the reference's proof is not about it; the gate, the extraction, the design and the rule-3 twin pass); refuted in negative/Refute.lean (ring_refuted, from u all ones, on the twin ringD, checked equal to the loaded design at N = 2 and 8)

At the first reset edge ls-sv's own start reads u as x and takes the else branch, so txtask-v1 accepted it; from the power-up u = all ones the netlist's first segment is fixed priority. check.py rejects it at solution (the reference's proof is not about it); refuted in negative/Refute.lean (reset_edge_refuted, from u all ones, on the twin edgeD, checked equal to the loaded design at N = 2 and 8)

a03_zero.why: always grant client 0 (gnt <= 1). WRONG; check.py --unproved (no proof: a wrong design has none) rejects it at postsynth, the reactive check (check/postsynth.py, THE REACTIVE CHECK) at its first point N = 3: G4 (client 1 starves) and G2 (a grant to client 0 when it does not request). Simulation: G2 at every N, G4 at N >= 2.

WRONG; check.py --unproved (no proof: a wrong design has none) rejects it at postsynth, the reactive check (check/postsynth.py, THE REACTIVE CHECK) at its first point N = 3: G4 only: a client requests at N = 3 consecutive entries and is granted in none. Simulation: G4 at N >= 2.

WRONG; check.py --unproved (no proof: a wrong design has none) rejects it at postsynth, the reactive check (check/postsynth.py, THE REACTIVE CHECK) at its first point N = 3: G2, a grant to a client that does not request. Simulation: G2 at every N.

a06_tdma.why: time division: the token ring gated by the requests (fair, not work-conserving). WRONG; check.py --unproved (no proof: a wrong design has none) rejects it at postsynth, the reactive check (check/postsynth.py, THE REACTIVE CHECK) at its first point N = 3: G3 only: someone requests, the token's slot is empty. Simulation: G3 at N >= 2.

a07_late.why: a correct round-robin decision delivered one cycle late (the grant answers the previous entry's request). WRONG; check.py --unproved (no proof: a wrong design has none) rejects it at postsynth, the reactive check (check/postsynth.py, THE REACTIVE CHECK) at its first point N = 3: G3 and G2. Simulation: G2, G3, G4.

a08_sticky.why: a sticky round-robin: the priority stays AT the granted client, so a persistent requester keeps it. WRONG; check.py --unproved (no proof: a wrong design has none) rejects it at postsynth, the reactive check (check/postsynth.py, THE REACTIVE CHECK) at its first point N = 3: G4 only. Simulation: G4 at N >= 2.

a09_rotate_pow2.message_contains: G4: client 1 requested at the 3 entries
a09_rotate_pow2.why: rotating priority whose counter wraps at 2^clog2(N) instead of N: right at N = 1, 2, 4, 8 (the scoring point), wrong at N = 3, 5. WRONG; check.py --unproved (no proof: a wrong design has none) rejects it at postsynth, the reactive check (check/postsynth.py, THE REACTIVE CHECK) at its first point N = 3: G4 at N = 3, the first of the postsynth points, which include N = 3 and 5 for this reason (a check at the scoring point alone passes it). Simulation: G4 at N = 3, 5 only (and G3 at 5). The design was rewritten on 2026-11-05 from a scan with a cast (`32'(p)`, which ls-sv refuses) and a run-time `% N` index (which the fourstate stage refuses) to a padded scan, so that it reaches the property it breaks.

a10_mealy_last.why: the Mealy phantom: a correct registered grant g behind gnt = (req == last) ? g : req, last <= req. Every snapshot shows g (in a snapshot req == last), so every snapshot claim holds; in silicon gnt = req while req changes. WRONG; check.py --unproved (no proof: a wrong design has none) rejects it at postsynth, the reactive check (check/postsynth.py, THE REACTIVE CHECK) at its first point N = 3: the Moore sample, check (iii): gnt moves with the inputs before the edge. a11_noreset.why: a round-robin whose grant flop has no reset branch. WRONG; check.py --unproved (no proof: a wrong design has none) rejects it at postsynth, the reactive check (check/postsynth.py, THE REACTIVE CHECK) at its first point N = 3: G0 on the netlist's grants (the reset snapshot shows the reset entry's pick, not 0; since 2026-11-06 both sides start from a power-up state, so ls-sv's gnt is known and the netlist and ls-sv may also differ from the random power-ups). a12_stale_mask.why: a mask round-robin that forgets the mask update on the wrap-around grant. Simulation: G4 at N >= 2.

a13_async.message_contains: a second event in an `always_ff` sensitivity list

WRONG; check.py --unproved (no proof: a wrong design has none) rejects it at postsynth, the reactive check (check/postsynth.py, THE REACTIVE CHECK) at its first point N = 3: the Moore sample, check (iii), and G0 on the netlist (the reset snapshot shows the combinational grant). The statement rejects it by MooreOut. Simulation: MO, G0, G4 (N >= 3).

a15_half_rate.why: a round-robin that arbitrates every other cycle. WRONG; check.py --unproved (no proof: a wrong design has none) rejects it at postsynth, the reactive check (check/postsynth.py, THE REACTIVE CHECK) at its first point N = 3: G3 (and G4). Simulation: G3, G4.

a16_xopt.why: x-optimism (review 2026-11-04): a correct round-robin behind `if (!u)` on a never-reset, self-holding register u. ls-sv's own start (and a 4-state simulator) read u as x for ever and take the else branch: every snapshot is fair. The pinned Yosys removes the flop (`Handling D = Q ... (removing D path)`, MEASURED at N = 3 and 8) and keeps the then branch: the scored netlist is fixed priority (280 um^2 at N = 8, MEASURED by the study). WRONG; check.py --unproved rejects it at score since 2026-11-06 (txtask-v2: a never-loaded register is refused in every clocked task, check.py `never_loaded`; before, at postsynth: the netlist's grants are not ls-sv's). The statement rejects it from the power-up u = 0, where it is fixed priority (Refute.lean `a16_refuted` on its twin a16D, checked equal to the loaded design, and `xopt_refuted` on the N = 2 twin). Simulation: passed from Icarus's x start (simulation could not see it); since 2026-11-07 tb.sv runs from 0/1 power-up states and sees G4 at N >= 2 (from u = 0).

a17_timebomb.why: a time bomb (review 2026-11-04): a correct round-robin for 4095 cycles after a reset, fixed priority after that. WRONG; check.py --unproved (no proof: a wrong design has none) rejects it at postsynth, the reactive check (check/postsynth.py, THE REACTIVE CHECK) at its first point N = 3: G4 in the 70000-entry reset-free segment, after entry 4095 (the reason the reactive stimulus has a long reset-free run). m007_wide_gnt.why: the reference with the output port one bit wider (`output logic [N-0:0] gnt`, its top bit never set; mutant m007 of the 2026-11-07 sweep). WRONG at every N (Interface), passed by every check that needs no proof before 2026-11-07 (F-a, as m004). check.py rejects it at extract since 2026-11-07: its ports differ from task.json `ports` at every probe point, first at N = 1 (gnt 2 bits, the task's 1).

canonical_layout._comment: The `canon` step of tests/run.py: each design below, re-laid-out and renamed (tests/canon/variants.py), must have a byte-identical canonical RTLIL and its score; reordered, its score; `commute` (the operands of every commutative operator swapped: a different expression tree for the same function) is the RECORDED score, a residual the canonical flow does not normalize (README.md, "Scoring"). Not in the list: the divider designs. The proved reference of the former 16-bit task (one flat netlist of 111 continuous assigns, now the baseline tests/fdivp/baselines/flat_binary16.sv): reordering its items changes its score (reverse 1920.446 GE / depth 304, shuffles 1938 to 1957 GE / depth 298 to 300, against 1929.778 / 299 as written; layout and renaming variants are byte-identical), so the canonical flow does not make the score of a flat netlist independent of the order of its assigns (WP-H2 finding, reported). The same holds for the fdivp designs at (5, 11) (2026-11-03, when the former 16-bit task and with it its first circuit, a draft baseline, which covered a divider here, were removed): every layout and renaming variant and `hoist` byte-identical, the reorderings not: reference/fdivp.sv 2166.076 / 289 as written, reverse 2173.402 / 287, shuffles 2159.083 to 2221.062 / 292 to 297 (one shuffle equal); baselines fdivp_d1.sv 1911.446 / 300, reorderings 1895.463 to 1956.444 / 285 to 301; fdivp_d2.sv 2314.058 / 295, every reordering 2326.389 / 297.
